hints.text: Conditions string contains codes separated by spaces where target codes begin with DIAB1.

hints.title: Boundary Pattern Cases
hints.text: A code may appear at the very start of the string or preceded by a space character.

hints.title: Combining Like Conditions
hints.text: filter using where conditions like "DIAB1%" or conditions like "% DIAB1%".

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT patient_id, patient_name, conditions
FROM Patients
WHERE conditions LIKE 'DIAB1%' OR conditions LIKE '% DIAB1%';
```

complexity.notes: Full table scan checking substring matches for each record.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Searching for "%DIAB1%" without leading space matches false positives like SADIAB100.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual like clauses provide optimal portability without requiring regex engine overhead.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling prefix and word boundaries correctly without matching internal substrings.

solutions.approach: Dual Like Clause for Word Boundaries

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def find_patients(patients: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    cond = patients['conditions'].fillna('')
    mask = cond.str.startswith('DIAB1') | cond.str.contains(r' DIAB1', regex=False)
    return patients[mask]
